beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Seth types: an agent that audits Unity scripts and refactors them and writes the missing tests and generates a CLAUDE.md. Refused. Two ands — four projects dressed as one. He stares at the screen. He thinks about which one he actually wants. Fourteen minutes later he types twenty-eight words. One sentence. No code. That sentence is the most valuable thing he writes this semester.

beats.narration_text: The one-sentence constraint is not about writing style. It is an elevator test for whether you know what you're building. A sentence with two ands is two systems dressed as one — different users, different inputs, different done-conditions. The refusal forces the decision that the list of features was deferring. Seth had thought he was building one thing. He was postponing a choice. The fourteen minutes is not wasted time. It is the essential work.

beats.narration_text: The sentence that passes names one system, one user, one done-condition — and contains no ands. The sentence that passes is the moment you take ownership of the project's conceptual integrity. Everything Claude produces from there gets measured against that sentence. The sentence costs fourteen minutes. Skipping it costs the build.
